title: The tree that bleeds and lives
hookLine: strike a great tree anywhere and it lives; why Hindus say the self does not die
carry: the body dies; the self does not
last: SAMUDRA — WE COME FROM BEING, AND GO BACK.

lines: AN OLD TREE WITH A SCAR.
IT BLED, AND IT'S STILL STANDING.
cards: Find an old tree with a scar: where a branch was cut, or a car hit it, or someone carved initials years ago. Often you'll see where the sap ran, dried now into a hard, shiny crust. The tree bled.
And it's still standing, still leafing out every spring. Next to it, maybe, one branch is gray and bare, and never came back. Same tree.
One part alive, one part not. Uddalaka points his son to a great tree.

teach.h: STRIKE IT: IT BLEEDS, BUT LIVES.
teach.b: If someone were to strike this great tree at its root, my dear, Uddalaka says, it would bleed sap, but it would live. Strike it in the middle, it would bleed, but live. Strike it at the top, it would bleed, but live.
Filled through and through by the living self, the jiva atman, it stands, drinking in water, rejoicing.

teach.h: LIFE LEAVES A BRANCH; IT DRIES.
teach.b: But if life leaves one branch, that branch dries up. If it leaves a second, or a third, they dry up. If it leaves the whole tree, the whole tree dries up.
Then the line that turns it toward his son. In the same way, my dear, understand this: the body dies when life leaves it. But life does not die.
Look at the order. The body depends on the self, not the other way around. A dry branch isn't the death of life; it's life leaving that branch.

teach.h: THE ATMAN IS NOT THE BODY.
teach.b: This is one of Hinduism's central teachings: the atman, the self, is not the body, and it does not die.

The Bhagavad Gita says it too, in its second chapter: as a person puts off worn-out clothes and puts on new ones, the self leaves a worn-out body. That is the hope many Hindu families hold onto at a funeral.

teach.h: THE BODY DIES. THE SELF DOES NOT.
teach.b: And they say: the body has died; the one we love has not. Then the refrain once more: you are that, Shvetaketu.

how: At Hindu deathbeds and funerals, families may recite or reflect on scriptures that teach that the self does not die with the body, from the Upanishads to the Bhagavad Gita's second chapter.

o: Uddalaka's picture of a body filled with life
a family tree, tracing who descends from whom
the beam a king's builders carved for a palace

games.q: what's inside the lesson — tap the pairs.

s: Uddalaka says life sits in the tree's root only
root, middle, top: strike it anywhere and it bleeds, but lives.
the Bhagavad Gita says the self puts off a worn-out body like worn-out clothes
chapter two: the self is not the body, and does not die with it.
the tree stands drinking in water, rejoicing
filled through and through by the living self.

games.q: at a Hindu funeral, someone reads from the Gita's second chapter. by today's teaching, why that chapter?
o: it teaches that the self, the atman, doesn't die with the body.
it's a list of rules for funerals.
it says grief is wrong, so nobody should cry.
games.why: like Uddalaka's tree: the body dies when life leaves it, but the self does not. families still grieve; they grieve with hope.

practice: Bring your attention to your feet, your roots, and feel something alive there: warmth, tingling, a pulse.
Move up through your belly and chest, where the breath moves, to your face and scalp, the same life from root to crown, and rest in it the way the tree stands, drinking in water.

wordCard.voice: The tree. Uddalaka's great tree, filled by the living self: wounded, it lives; when life leaves, it dries; the body dies, but the self does not.

orig.note: Sanskrit jīva: living, a living being. the tree is filled by the jīva ātman, the living self.

carryVoice: Your line: the body dies; the self does not. That's day three hundred forty-seven.

sources.ref: Chandogya Upanishad 6.11.1–3 (the tree; the body dies, life does not; the refrain)
Bhagavad Gita 2.20, 2.22 (the self is not slain when the body is slain; worn-out clothes and a worn-out body)
